Do NOT anchor on 'nothing can be done because she woke up with it' — wake-up stroke with favorable perfusion mismatch and LVO is a thrombectomy indication
Do NOT give IV tPA before non-contrast CT excludes intracranial hemorrhage
Do NOT aggressively lower blood pressure below 140-150 mmHg systolic in the acute phase — risks worsening perfusion to the large penumbra
Do NOT skip CTA before thrombectomy — LVO must be documented prior to endovascular intervention

Obtain non-contrast CT head FIRST to exclude intracranial hemorrhage before any reperfusion decision
Obtain CT angiography to document LVO (right MCA M1 occlusion) — LVO documentation is mandatory before mechanical thrombectomy

Do NOT administer IV tPA based on unknown onset time alone — document that standard IV tPA is contraindicated when LKW exceeds 4.5 hours without MRI DWI-FLAIR mismatch evidence of acute onset

key_clinical_evidence: Wake-up stroke with unknown onset time places the patient outside the standard IV tPA window (4.5h); however, unknown onset time does NOT preclude mechanical thrombectomy in the extended window when perfusion imaging demonstrates favorable mismatch

DAWN (6-24h) and DEFUSE-3 (6-16h) trials established that imaging-based patient selection — small infarct core with large salvageable penumbra — identifies patients who benefit from mechanical thrombectomy far beyond the conventional time window

This case meets DEFUSE-3 criteria: ischemic core 18 mL (below 70 mL threshold), mismatch ratio 6.6 (above 1.8 threshold), mismatch volume 100 mL (above 15 mL threshold) — mechanical thrombectomy is indicated

Laterality check: right MCA M1 occlusion causes contralateral left-sided deficits (left dense hemiplegia, left hemisensory loss, left neglect, left hemianopia) and ipsilateral gaze deviation to the RIGHT (toward the lesion) — there is NO aphasia because the right hemisphere is non-dominant for language in this right-handed patient

The 'wake-up stroke / nothing to do' anchoring heuristic is the primary red herring — the correct clinical response is to proceed urgently to perfusion imaging and thrombectomy evaluation, not to default to supportive care
FLAIR-positive DWI infarct confirms lesion age >4.5 hours, excluding MRI-guided tPA (WAKE-UP criteria); this reinforces that thrombectomy, not tPA, is the appropriate reperfusion strategy

Left atrial enlargement on initial ECG plus newly detected paroxysmal AF on Holter monitoring identifies a likely cardioembolic mechanism — anticoagulation (not antiplatelet) becomes the secondary prevention cornerstone once hemorrhagic transformation risk is acceptable
Tier per the July 2026 clinical review: Non-contrast CT is the required first-line study in the acute window; MRI adds tissue-based selection and is not mandatory for the diagnosis.

AHA/ASA 2026 sequencing: glucose is checked before thrombolysis, but routine CBC/coagulation results are not awaited without a reason to expect abnormality; ECG/troponin do not delay reperfusion, and CTA/CTP do not wait for creatinine.

clinical_pearls: Wake-up stroke does not mean 'no treatment' — the extended thrombectomy window (DAWN 6-24h, DEFUSE-3 6-16h) was specifically designed for unknown-onset presentations with favorable perfusion mismatch
The critical metric is not the clock: it is the ratio of ischemic core to salvageable penumbra. Core <70 mL + mismatch ratio >1.8 + mismatch volume >15 mL are the DEFUSE-3 imaging thresholds

Right MCA M1 occlusion produces leftward deficits (left hemiplegia, left neglect, left hemianopia) and RIGHTWARD cortical gaze deviation — do not confuse with left MCA stroke where gaze deviates left and aphasia is expected
Left atrial enlargement on the admission ECG is a structural risk marker for paroxysmal AF; normal sinus rhythm on a resting tracing does not exclude AF as the embolic source
metadata.difficulty_description: Diagnostic puzzle — wake-up stroke with unknown last-known-well (LKW) creates anchoring toward 'no reperfusion possible'; the critical insight is that DAWN/DEFUSE-3 criteria enable extended-window mechanical thrombectomy using perfusion mismatch (small core 18 mL, large penumbra 118 mL, mismatch ratio 6.6) despite unknown onset. IV tPA is contraindicated. Laterality is right MCA M1 occlusion causing left hemiplegia, left neglect, and rightward gaze deviation with no aphasia. Paroxysmal AF identified only on Holter monitoring despite initial sinus ECG.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: Wake-up stroke with unknown LKW anchoring red herring, required perfusion-mismatch reasoning for extended-window thrombectomy (DAWN/DEFUSE-3), multiple required tools (CT x2, CTP, labs, ECG, literature, drug check, MRI, echo, Holter, carotid duplex), paroxysmal AF only on Holter not initial ECG.

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Esperanza Delgado is a 66-year-old right-handed Hispanic woman with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia who is brought to the emergency department by her husband at 07:40 after he found her unable to rise from bed when he woke up. The husband reports that she was entirely at her baseline when they went to sleep at approximately 23:00 the previous evening — conversational, ambulating normally, and without any neurologic complaints. He awoke at approximately 07:10 and found her sitting on the edge of the bed, unable to stand, with her left arm hanging at her side and her eyes and head turned to the right. She was alert and speaking coherently but appeared unaware that anything was wrong with her left side. He immediately called 911. The patient herself denies any preceding symptoms — no headache, no visual symptoms, no palpitations, no chest pain, no tongue-biting or incontinence overnight. She is unaware of her left-sided weakness and reports feeling 'fine' other than being 'tired.' There was no witnessed seizure activity, no fever or recent illness, no trauma, no chiropractic manipulation. She has not taken any anticoagulants. She takes no aspirin or other antiplatelet agents. She has no prior history of stroke or TIA. Given that onset was unwitnessed during sleep, with the last known well established at bedtime approximately 8 hours before emergency department arrival, the clinical team must determine whether the patient qualifies for any acute reperfusion therapy. Standard IV tPA is not administered because onset time is unknown, placing the patient definitively outside the 4.5-hour window without imaging evidence of early onset. The attending neurologist activates the stroke team and orders urgent imaging including non-contrast CT, CTA, and CT perfusion to characterize the extent of ischemia and salvageable penumbra for potential extended-window mechanical thrombectomy decision.

Time from last known well to emergency department arrival: approximately 8 hours (well established at 23:00, deficits discovered at 07:10, arrived ED 07:40).
neurological_exam.coordination: Unable to test left side given plegia. Right-sided finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin intact.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils 3 mm bilaterally, reactive. Forced conjugate deviation of gaze to the RIGHT; cannot voluntarily bring eyes past midline to the left. Left homonymous hemianopia on confrontation. Left central facial droop with flattening of the left nasolabial fold, sparing the forehead.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented to person and place. Inattentive — unable to complete serial 7s; makes significant errors on months backward. Marked left-sided neglect: extinction of left visual and tactile stimuli on double-simultaneous testing; left personal neglect with failure to acknowledge left-sided body parts. Speech is fluent, articulate, and prosodically normal with intact repetition and naming — no aphasia.
neurological_exam.motor: Left upper extremity: 0/5 throughout — arm plegic, no voluntary movement against gravity. Left lower extremity: 1/5 proximal, 0/5 distal — flaccid with trace hip flexion only. Right upper and lower extremities: 5/5 throughout. Left pronator posturing noted at rest.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Left upper extremity hyporeflexic acutely (2+). Left lower extremity 3+ patellar and Achilles. Left Babinski upgoing. Right plantar flexor. Right reflexes 2+ throughout.
neurological_exam.sensory: Dense left hemisensory loss to light touch, pinprick, and proprioception. No response to pain on the left. Right side intact.
